question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=8-(x+2)^{2}.$ For which of the following values of $k$ does the intermediate value theorem guarantee that $f(x)=k$ has a solution on the interval $x\in [-2,1]?$
question.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is continuous on $[-2,1],$ so the intermediate value theorem guarantees that $f(x)=k$ has a solution for each value of $k$ between $f(-2)$ and $f(1).$

Since $f(-2)=8$ and $f(1)=-1,$ we must have 
$k\in [-1,8].$

Among the given options, only $k=5$ belongs to the interval $[-1,8].$
